stats.description: Values below are fictional sample data.

ec2.name: Amazon EC2
ec2.description: Virtual servers you manage yourself, for full control over the OS and runtime.

ecsFargate.name: Amazon ECS Fargate
ecsFargate.description: Runs containers without managing servers — AWS handles the underlying infrastructure.

lambda.name: AWS Lambda
lambda.description: Runs code in response to events, with no servers to provision or manage.

rdsPostgres.name: Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL)
rdsPostgres.description: A managed relational database, with AWS handling patching, backups and failover.

dynamoDb.name: Amazon DynamoDB
dynamoDb.description: A managed NoSQL database built for consistent, low-latency access at any scale.

s3.name: Amazon S3
s3.description: Durable object storage for files, backups, static assets and data of any size.

efs.name: Amazon EFS
efs.description: A managed file system that multiple compute instances can mount at once.

vpc.name: Amazon VPC
vpc.description: An isolated network you control, where the rest of your architecture runs.

alb.name: Application Load Balancer
alb.description: Distributes incoming traffic across multiple compute targets for availability.

apiGateway.name: Amazon API Gateway
apiGateway.description: A managed front door for APIs, handling routing, throttling and authorization.

cloudfront.name: Amazon CloudFront
cloudfront.description: A content delivery network that caches content closer to users worldwide.

route53.name: Amazon Route 53
route53.description: A managed DNS service for routing traffic to your application's endpoints.

secretsManager.name: AWS Secrets Manager
secretsManager.description: Stores and rotates credentials so secrets never sit in code or config files.

kms.name: AWS KMS
kms.description: Manages encryption keys used to protect data across your AWS services.

waf.name: AWS WAF
waf.description: A web application firewall that filters malicious traffic before it reaches your app.

cloudwatch.name: Amazon CloudWatch
cloudwatch.description: Collects logs, metrics and alarms for observing how your architecture behaves.

sns.name: Amazon SNS
sns.description: Publishes notifications to many subscribers at once (fan-out messaging).

sqs.name: Amazon SQS
sqs.description: A managed queue that decouples services and smooths out traffic spikes.

eventBridge.name: Amazon EventBridge
eventBridge.description: Routes events between AWS services and applications based on rules.
